brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.

requirements.requirement: Holder for iron while it is switched on and hot
requirements.evidence: Not built. 3D printed plastic cannot safely hold a hot, powered soldering iron (heat/fire risk, melting, no heat-resistance verification). No suitable heat-resistant holder exists in configurator; system checks fit only.

requirements.requirement: Two bins for solder and spare tips (cold storage)
requirements.evidence: Built bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full holds solder reel prop, bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div2 with compartments holds tips/consumables (heap-standoffs-div3 as tips). Third bin with mug ring available for organization.
Provided bench-top organizer for cold materials only. Use a commercial ceramic/metal soldering iron stand for hot iron separate from this plastic organizer.

finish.summary: Built compact 3-cell bench organizer with bins for solder and spare tips, but declined hot-iron holder: holding a switched-on hot iron in printed plastic is unsafe (melting/fire risk) and configurator cannot verify heat safety. Use a proper metal/ceramic iron stand alongside this organizer for cold storage.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your soldering station needs a hot-iron holder — that’s not safe in printed plastic, so I’ll sort a workable compromise and check your bench.
I can’t make a holder for a powered-on iron, but I’ll set up the cold storage you need.
